# google_assured_workloads_v2_workload

An Assured Workloads V2 workload applies a compliance framework, such as a
Data Boundary framework, and its cloud controls to a Google Cloud folder or
project.


To get more information about Workload, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/docs/reference/rest/v2/organizations.locations.workloads)
* How-to Guides
    * [Assured Workloads Overview](https://cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/docs/overview)

~> **Note:** Workloads have no project, so Assured Workloads attributes API quota and
billing to the client project of your credentials unless a billing project
is set. Set `billing_project` and `user_project_override = true` in the
provider configuration to use a project where the Assured Workloads API is
enabled. `resource_config` is not returned by the API, so it is not
populated on import.


## Example Usage - Assured Workloads V2 Workload Basic


```hcl
provider "google" {
  user_project_override = true
  billing_project       = "my-project-name"
}

resource "google_project" "target" {
  project_id      = "aw-target"
  name            = "aw-target"
  org_id          = "123456789"
  billing_account = "000000-0000000-0000000-000000"
  deletion_policy = "DELETE"
}

resource "google_assured_workloads_v2_workload" "workload" {
  organization = "123456789"
  location     = "us-east4"
  workload_id  = "example-workload"
  description  = "US Data Boundary workload"

  resource_config {
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `resource_config` -
  (Required)
  The target Google Cloud folder or project where the compliance controls
  are deployed. Exactly one target must be specified.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_resource_config).

* `framework` -
  (Required)
  The compliance framework applied by the workload.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_framework).

* `cloud_control_configs` -
  (Required)
  The cloud control configurations enforced on the workload. Every cloud
  control of the framework revision that supports the deployment mode must
  be listed, with the revision used by the framework: in monitor mode every
  control that supports `DETECTIVE` is deployed in `DETECTIVE` mode, and in
  monitor and prevent mode every control that supports `PREVENTIVE` is
  deployed in `PREVENTIVE` mode and the remaining controls that support
  `DETECTIVE` are deployed in `DETECTIVE` mode. Controls can't be moved from
  `PREVENTIVE` back to `DETECTIVE`.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs).

* `organization` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the parent organization of the workload, for example `123456789`.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the workload, for example `us-east4`. Requests are
  sent to the regional `{location}-assuredworkloads.googleapis.com`
  endpoint for this location.

* `workload_id` -
  (Required)
  The user-assigned identifier for the workload, which must be unique within
  the parent organization and location. It can contain only letters,
  numbers, hyphens and underscores.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  The user-provided description of the workload.

* `kaj_enrollment_type` -
  (Optional)
  The Key Access Transparency choice for the workload. Possible values are
  `KEY_ACCESS_TRANSPARENCY_ENABLED` and `KEY_ACCESS_TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED`.
  It can be set only for frameworks that support Key Access Transparency
  and only when at least one cloud control is in `PREVENTIVE` mode. If
  omitted, the service enables Key Access Transparency for eligible
  frameworks deployed in `PREVENTIVE` mode.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_resource_config"></a>The `resource_config` block supports:

* `existing_project` -
  (Optional)
  An existing Google Cloud project, in the format
  `projects/{project_id_or_number}`.

* `existing_folder` -
  (Optional)
  An existing Google Cloud folder, in the format `folders/{folder}`.

* `new_project_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration to provision a new Google Cloud project. Deleting the
  workload does not delete the provisioned project.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_resource_config_new_project_config).

* `new_folder_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration to provision a new Google Cloud folder. Deleting the
  workload does not delete the provisioned folder.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_resource_config_new_folder_config).


<a name="nested_resource_config_new_project_config"></a>The `new_project_config` block supports:

* `parent` -
  (Required)
  The parent resource where the project is created, in the format
  `organizations/{organization}` or `folders/{folder}`.

* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the new project.

* `billing_account` -
  (Required)
  The billing account to link to the new project, in the format
  `billingAccounts/{billing_account}` or `{billing_account}`.

<a name="nested_resource_config_new_folder_config"></a>The `new_folder_config` block supports:

* `parent` -
  (Required)
  The parent resource where the folder is created, in the format
  `organizations/{organization}` or `folders/{folder}`.

* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the new folder.

<a name="nested_framework"></a>The `framework` block supports:

* `framework` -
  (Required)
  The resource name of the Compliance Manager framework, in the format
  `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/frameworks/{framework}`.
  The framework location must match the workload location (`eu` for
  `europe` workloads).

* `major_revision_id` -
  (Optional)
  The major revision of the framework. If omitted, the latest revision
  is used. The revision can only be increased in place, and only for
  built-in frameworks.

<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs"></a>The `cloud_control_configs` block supports:

* `cloud_control` -
  (Required)
  The resource name of the cloud control, in the format
  `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/cloudControls/{cloud_control}`.
  The location must match the workload location.

* `cloud_control_revision` -
  (Required)
  The major revision of the cloud control.

* `enforcement_mode` -
  (Required)
  The enforcement mode of the cloud control. Possible values are
  `PREVENTIVE` and `DETECTIVE`. See the
  [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/docs/reference/rest/v2/organizations.locations.workloads)
  for the current list of values.

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  The parameters of the cloud control configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters).


<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters"></a>The `parameters` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the parameter.

* `parameter_value` -
  (Required)
  The value of the parameter. Exactly one value must be set.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value).


<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value"></a>The `parameter_value` block supports:

* `string_value` -
  (Optional)
  A string value.

* `bool_value` -
  (Optional)
  A boolean value.

* `number_value` -
  (Optional)
  A double value.

* `string_list_value` -
  (Optional)
  A list of strings.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_string_list_value).

* `oneof_value` -
  (Optional)
  A sub-parameter value.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_oneof_value).


<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_string_list_value"></a>The `string_list_value` block supports:

* `values` -
  (Required)
  The strings in the list.

<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_oneof_value"></a>The `oneof_value` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the sub-parameter.

* `parameter_value` -
  (Required)
  The value of the sub-parameter. Exactly one value must be set.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_oneof_value_parameter_value).


<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_oneof_value_parameter_value"></a>The `parameter_value` block supports:

* `string_value` -
  (Optional)
  A string value.

* `bool_value` -
  (Optional)
  A boolean value.

* `number_value` -
  (Optional)
  A double value.

* `string_list_value` -
  (Optional)
  A list of strings.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_oneof_value_parameter_value_string_list_value).


<a name="nested_cloud_control_configs_parameters_parameter_value_oneof_value_parameter_value_string_list_value"></a>The `string_list_value` block supports:

* `values` -
  (Required)
  The strings in the list.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `organizations/{{organization}}/locations/{{location}}/workloads/{{workload_id}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the workload, in the format
  `organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/workloads/{workload}`.

* `computed_target_resource` -
  The resolved target resource, in the format `projects/{project_number}`
  or `folders/{folder_id}`.

* `target_resource_display_name` -
  The display name of the target resource.

* `state` -
  The current lifecycle state of the workload, for example `ACTIVE`.

* `create_time` -
  The time the workload was created.

* `update_time` -
  The time the workload was last updated.

* `etag` -
  An opaque concurrency control token calculated by the server.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 30 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 30 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 30 minutes.

## Import


Workload can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `organizations/{{organization}}/locations/{{location}}/workloads/{{workload_id}}`
* `{{organization}}/{{location}}/{{workload_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import Workload using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    organization = "<-required value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    workloadId = "<-required value->"
  }
  to = google_assured_workloads_v2_workload.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import Workload using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "organizations/{{organization}}/locations/{{location}}/workloads/{{workload_id}}"
  to = google_assured_workloads_v2_workload.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), Workload can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_assured_workloads_v2_workload.default organizations/{{organization}}/locations/{{location}}/workloads/{{workload_id}}
$ terraform import google_assured_workloads_v2_workload.default {{organization}}/{{location}}/{{workload_id}}
```
